narrative.overview:
Fryday Chef looks like the hour when a Savannah sky turns violet and the plates come out. The page is a twilight gradient, lilac at the top edge warming to peach at the horizon, and every surface sits on it like linen on a porch table: white, warm, slightly translucent, lifted by a soft plum-tinted haze rather than a hard shadow. Nothing is urgent. Spacing is generous, corners are round, type is set wide and unhurried.

The precision lives inside that calm. Recipe steps are numbered tiles with tabular figures, checkable boxes, and a reasoning line under every instruction. Restaurant pages carry a knife-icon rating and tap-to-highlight must-try chips. Uppercase tracked labels run through eyebrows, navigation, buttons, and dates as the one crisp element in an otherwise soft system. The hospitality is the atmosphere; the technique is the furniture.

Two looks are confirmed anti-references. Fryday Chef is never the ad-stuffed recipe blog: no preamble before the recipe, no jump-to-recipe button, no sidebar. It is never farmhouse Pinterest: no kraft paper, chalkboard, script type, or "gather" signage.
keyCharacteristics: Twilight gradient page background, lilac to peach, with faint radial glows
Translucent white and peach-linen surfaces, every one rounded 12 to 24px
Ambient plum-tinted shadows that float surfaces without ranking them
Roboto Slab headlines over Roboto body, with tracked uppercase labels as the system's crisp counterpoint
Soft Iris violet as the single interactive signal: links, active states, checkboxes, step numbers, underlines
Cook-along furniture: numbered step tiles, checklists, completion badges

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Soft Iris is the only color that means "interactive". No second accent is introduced for emphasis; warmth comes from peach surfaces, not from a second hue of action.

rules.name: The Plum Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted Dusk Plum (rgb 47 36 58), never neutral black. A grey shadow on this palette reads as dirt.

rules.name: The Translucent Surface Rule
rules.body: White surfaces sit at 85 to 95% opacity so the gradient beneath softens them. Opaque white is reserved for the smallest fills: chips, the search field, the reset button.

rules.name: The Slab Headline Rule
rules.body: Every h1 and h2 is Roboto Slab. Inner page titles (recipe, restaurant, note, travel detail) currently render in plain Roboto at browser default size; that is a gap against this rule, not the system.

rules.name: The Tracked Label Rule
rules.body: Anything uppercase is tracked at least 0.16em. Uppercase without tracking does not exist here.

rules.name: The Haze Rule
rules.body: Shadows are atmosphere. They never rise above 24% opacity, never shrink below 18px blur, and never choose a surface's importance.

dos: Do use Soft Iris for every interactive signal and nothing else; it is the One Signal.
Do tint every shadow Dusk Plum and keep it in the Ambient vocabulary.
Do set every surface at 85 to 95% white or a white-to-Peach-Linen gradient so the dusk gradient shows through.
Do keep uppercase labels tracked at 0.16em or wider.
Do set every h1 and h2 in Roboto Slab, including inner page titles.
Do keep the whole step tile and the whole card as the click target.
Do keep recipe furniture (checkbox, number tile, detail line, completion badge) intact and persistent; it is the cook-along mechanism.
Do frame every image with the 1px Lilac Line and its container radius.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue for emphasis; use Peach Linen surfaces for warmth instead.
Don't use pure black or neutral grey anywhere, including shadows.
Don't add preamble, a jump-to-recipe button, a sidebar, or ad slots; the recipe is the page.
Don't reach for kraft paper, chalkboard, script fonts, or farmhouse signage.
Don't use sharp corners; the smallest radius in the system is 12px on the number tile.
Don't spread Terracotta Mark or Ember beyond the favicon and step alerts.
Don't let a button fall back to the browser font; set font: inherit.
